answer:
**Answer**

Celebrity Big Brother is a CBS‑produced series – it premiered on **CBS on February 7, 2018** and completed its first season on February 25, 2018.  
It has *not* been scheduled to air on the other major New‑York‑based broadcaster, **NBC**. As of now, there are no announced plans for Celebrity Big Brother to move to NBC, so the show’s launch date on NBC remains “not applicable.”

So there are two networks: ABC and the other major broadcaster based in NY. The other one is NBC? Wait, NBC is based in New York. Wait, ABC also has a major presence in NY. The question: "network which, along with ABC and the network which aired Law of the Plainsman, is the other major broadcaster based in NY." Actually Law of the Plainsman starred Jon Hall and John Carroll and was in 1945-1946. It was produced by "Nelson M. Kaufman" for the "Warner Bros. # Law of the Plainsman
TV Series TV-PG 1959 1 season 12 episodes
Watch Now S1 E1 Signal Save Beam
Drama Western
**Director**Douglas Heyes, Jerry Hopper, Richard Whorf
One of the first network television series to feature a Native American as its lead character. Deputy U.S. Marshal Sam Buckhart, an Apache educated at Harvard, keeps the peace in 1879 New Mexico Territory, facing outlaws, lynch mobs and prejudice in this acclaimed NBC western from the producers of The Rifleman. Free with ads.

TV Series TV-PG 1959 1 season 12 episodes
Watch Now S1 E1 Signal Save Beam
Drama Western
**Director**Douglas Heyes, Jerry Hopper, Richard Whorf
One of the first network television series to feature a Native American as its lead character. Deputy U.S. Marshal Sam Buckhart, an Apache educated at Harvard, keeps the peace in 1879 New Mexico Territory, facing outlaws, lynch mobs and prejudice in this acclaimed NBC western from the producers of The Rifleman. Free with ads.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Digital cover art used for the first season
_Celebrity Big Brother_, also known as _Big Brother: Celebrity Edition_, is the American adaptation of the reality competition television franchise _Celebrity Big Brother_, which was created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBB1-Schedule-1) The series premiered on CBS as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics on February 7, 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-2) The series has aired for two seasons and focuses on a group of celebrities, known as HouseGuests, that live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother house, with no contact from the outside world for approximately a month. The HouseGuests try to avoid eviction with the aim of being the last remaining HouseGuest in order to win a grand prize of $250,000. Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan (Lim Jahey) serve as executive producers and the show is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3)Julie Chen Moonves hosts the series, continuing a position she has held since _Big Brother_ premiered on CBS in 2000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3) It is filmed in Los Angeles.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-4)

Each season consists of thirteen episodes airing over a span of two and a half weeks.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBB1-Schedule-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3) All episodes are approximately 44 to 82 minutes, excluding commercials, and are broadcast in both high-definition and standard.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Eviction-1-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-6) Episodes are also available for download at the iTunes Store in standard and high definition and Amazon Video, with new episodes appearing the day after their live airings.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-iTunes-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Amazon-8) Recent episodes are available at CBS' official _Celebrity Big Brother_ website and the CBS App for a limited amount of time.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9) All episodes are available on CBS All Access along with the live Internet feed allowing subscribers to watch the HouseGuests while a season is in progress.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9)_Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark_ is a companion show that airs on Pop concurrent with each season.

_After Dark_ provides viewers the opportunity to watch the HouseGuests live for three hours per day.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9) In order to preserve the drama for television broadcasts, CBS does not webcast certain moments that transpire in the house, including competitions and the nomination and eviction process.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-11)
As of February 23,2022, 41 episodes of _Celebrity Big Brother_ have aired, concluding the third season.

_Celebrity Big Brother_ had a strong series premiere with the highest ratings since the premiere of _Big Brother 13_ on July 7, 2011. The series debuted to 7.27 million viewers with a 1.8/7 rating in the 18-49 demographic.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S1E1_Rating-62) The remainder of the first season was scheduled as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The first season finale aired on February 25, 2018 with 5.2 million viewers with a 1.4/5 rating in the 18-49 demographic coming in second behind the closing ceremony for the Olympics.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-63) The first season averaged 5.04 million viewers per episode.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S1AVG-64)

The second season premiere was down compared to the first season with 5.36 million viewers with a 1.4/6 in the 18-49 demographic.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S2E1_Rating-65) The eighth episode of the second season pulled in the lowest ratings of the season with 3.28 million viewers.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-66) The finale for the second season was watched by 3.87 million viewers which was below season average levels for the program.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S2E13_Rating-67) The second season averaged a total of 4.40 million viewers.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S2AVG-68)

Title: Celebrity Big Brother (American TV series)
Chunks: 9,10,11,12,13
### Differences from _Big Brother_
The live finale features the most changes when compared to the live finales from _Big Brother_. Five HouseGuests remained inside the House by the season finale instead of the regular three HouseGuests.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB2_Winner-22) Live finales of _Big Brother_ feature a three-part final Head of Household competition with the final eviction of the season in order to reduce the number of contestants inside the House down to two.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-23) The live finale for the celebrity season was re-tooled to feature the conclusion of the final 5 round (including a pre-recorded Power of Veto competition and live eviction) then the final Head of Household competition is played in one part where the Final Head of Household wins the power to evict two HouseGuests in order to reduce the number of contestants inside the House down to two.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
After the first season of the British version of _Big Brother_ proved to be a success in the ratings for Channel 4, the network collaborated with the BBC for the first British season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ in aid of Comic Relief. The season ran for a condensed run of eight days and featured six British celebrities moving into the house used for the first British season.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-24) Due to the success of the first celebrity edition, a second season was ordered and shown exclusively on Channel 4 in November 2002. The celebrity version took a two-year break before returning for its third season in 2005 and became a regular staple alongside the regular British version. Starting with the third season, the show began to feature celebrities outside the United Kingdom alongside well-known British celebrities. Many notable American celebrities have since taken part in the British version of _Celebrity Big Brother_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-GlobalTV-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-AmericansInUKCBB-2-26) American actor Gary Busey took part in the fourteenth season in the summer of 2014 and became the first American celebrity to win _Celebrity Big Brother_ in the United Kingdom.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-Gary_Wins-27)
Julie Chen Moonves has hosted the series since its premiere.

### Differences from _Big Brother_
An American version of _Celebrity Big Brother_ has been speculated since 2002, along with a celebrity version of _Survivor._[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-2002-1-28) In an interview, Julie Chen and then CEO of CBS Corporation Leslie Moonves revealed talks of a celebrity edition of _Big Brother_ as far back as _Big Brother 2._[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-29) It was rumored that CBS was looking to air a celebrity edition in the fall after _Big Brother 3_ with radio personality Howard Stern speculated as a possible Houseguest.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-2002-2-30) Chen revealed that Paris Hilton had agreed to do it and Roseanne Barr initially agreed to take part, but then backed out.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-29) Barr would later take part in another celebrity spin-off of _Big Brother_ called _Big Brother: Celebrity Hijack_ in the United Kingdom in 2008, where she watched over a group of non-celebrity housemates for a day, set tasks and talked to them in the Diary Room.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Roseanne-BBCH-31) Julie Chen announced on September 7, 2017, during a live double eviction episode of _Big Brother 19_ that _Celebrity Big Brother_ would air sometime during the winter, before the twentieth season of _Big Brother_ in the summer of 2018.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-32)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
CBS confirmed that Chen would reprise her role as host for the celebrity edition with executive producers Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan returning. CBS also confirmed that the celebrity edition would be produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Press1-33) In an interview Chen revealed that her husband Les Moonves forced her to take a pay cut for _Celebrity Big Brother_ due to it being a condensed version.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-tvguide-34) Chen returned as the host for the second season now being credited as Julie Chen Moonves.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-JCReturn-35)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
Don Wollman and Clayton Halsey also reprises their roles as a co-executive producer and editor respectively.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ClosingCredits-36) Wollman also serves as the voice of Big Brother where he pre-records a series of statements that are played over the loud speakers inside the House. These range from asking HouseGuests to come to the Diary Room or reminding them they are not allowed to talk about production and their Diary Room sessions with other HouseGuests. Occasionally Wollman will make announcements to the HouseGuests that are not pre-recorded. Wollman's voice is primarily heard on the live Internet feeds while occasionally heard on the episodes.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-41) Halsey also serves as the narrator for the opening and closings of the broadcast episodes. In this role he recaps recent events that were aired in previous episodes during the opening while explaining what events will take place in future episodes during the closing.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Voices-38)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ClosingCredits2-37)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Digital cover art used for the first season
_Celebrity Big Brother_, also known as _Big Brother: Celebrity Edition_, is the American adaptation of the reality competition television franchise _Celebrity Big Brother_, which was created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBB1-Schedule-1) The series premiered on CBS as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics on February 7, 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-2) The series has aired for two seasons and focuses on a group of celebrities, known as HouseGuests, that live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother house, with no contact from the outside world for approximately a month. The HouseGuests try to avoid eviction with the aim of being the last remaining HouseGuest in order to win a grand prize of $250,000. Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan (Lim Jahey) serve as executive producers and the show is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3)Julie Chen Moonves hosts the series, continuing a position she has held since _Big Brother_ premiered on CBS in 2000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3) It is filmed in Los Angeles.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-4)
texts.1: Each season consists of thirteen episodes airing over a span of two and a half weeks.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBB1-Schedule-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3) All episodes are approximately 44 to 82 minutes, excluding commercials, and are broadcast in both high-definition and standard.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Eviction-1-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-6) Episodes are also available for download at the iTunes Store in standard and high definition and Amazon Video, with new episodes appearing the day after their live airings.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-iTunes-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Amazon-8) Recent episodes are available at CBS' official _Celebrity Big Brother_ website and the CBS App for a limited amount of time.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9) All episodes are available on CBS All Access along with the live Internet feed allowing subscribers to watch the HouseGuests while a season is in progress.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9)_Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark_ is a companion show that airs on Pop concurrent with each season.
texts.2:
_After Dark_ provides viewers the opportunity to watch the HouseGuests live for three hours per day.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9) In order to preserve the drama for television broadcasts, CBS does not webcast certain moments that transpire in the house, including competitions and the nomination and eviction process.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-11)
As of February 23,2022, 41 episodes of _Celebrity Big Brother_ have aired, concluding the third season.

texts.3: _Celebrity Big Brother_ had a strong series premiere with the highest ratings since the premiere of _Big Brother 13_ on July 7, 2011. The series debuted to 7.27 million viewers with a 1.8/7 rating in the 18-49 demographic.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S1E1_Rating-62) The remainder of the first season was scheduled as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The first season finale aired on February 25, 2018 with 5.2 million viewers with a 1.4/5 rating in the 18-49 demographic coming in second behind the closing ceremony for the Olympics.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-63) The first season averaged 5.04 million viewers per episode.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S1AVG-64)
texts.4:
The second season premiere was down compared to the first season with 5.36 million viewers with a 1.4/6 in the 18-49 demographic.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S2E1_Rating-65) The eighth episode of the second season pulled in the lowest ratings of the season with 3.28 million viewers.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-66) The finale for the second season was watched by 3.87 million viewers which was below season average levels for the program.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S2E13_Rating-67) The second season averaged a total of 4.40 million viewers.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S2AVG-68)

_Celebrity Big Brother_, also known as _Big Brother: Celebrity Edition_, is the American adaptation of the reality competition television franchise _Celebrity Big Brother_, which was created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBB1-Schedule-1) The series premiered on CBS as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics on February 7, 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-2) The series has aired for two seasons and focuses on a group of celebrities, known as HouseGuests, that live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother house, with no contact from the outside world for approximately a month. The HouseGuests try to avoid eviction with the aim of being the last remaining HouseGuest in order to win a grand prize of $250,000. Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan (Lim Jahey) serve as executive producers and the show is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3)Julie Chen Moonves hosts the series, continuing a position she has held since _Big Brother_ premiered on CBS in 2000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3) It is filmed in Los Angeles.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-4)

Each season consists of thirteen episodes airing over a span of two and a half weeks.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBB1-Schedule-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-3) All episodes are approximately 44 to 82 minutes, excluding commercials, and are broadcast in both high-definition and standard.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Eviction-1-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-6) Episodes are also available for download at the iTunes Store in standard and high definition and Amazon Video, with new episodes appearing the day after their live airings.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-iTunes-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Amazon-8) Recent episodes are available at CBS' official _Celebrity Big Brother_ website and the CBS App for a limited amount of time.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9) All episodes are available on CBS All Access along with the live Internet feed allowing subscribers to watch the HouseGuests while a season is in progress.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9)_Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark_ is a companion show that airs on Pop concurrent with each season.

_After Dark_ provides viewers the opportunity to watch the HouseGuests live for three hours per day.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-Coverage-9) In order to preserve the drama for television broadcasts, CBS does not webcast certain moments that transpire in the house, including competitions and the nomination and eviction process.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-11)
As of February 23,2022, 41 episodes of _Celebrity Big Brother_ have aired, concluding the third season.

The first season finale aired on February 25, 2018 with 5.2 million viewers with a 1.4/5 rating in the 18-49 demographic coming in second behind the closing ceremony for the Olympics.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-63) The first season averaged 5.04 million viewers per episode.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)_episodes#cite_note-S1AVG-64)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
The live finale features the most changes when compared to the live finales from _Big Brother_. Five HouseGuests remained inside the House by the season finale instead of the regular three HouseGuests.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB2_Winner-22) Live finales of _Big Brother_ feature a three-part final Head of Household competition with the final eviction of the season in order to reduce the number of contestants inside the House down to two.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-23) The live finale for the celebrity season was re-tooled to feature the conclusion of the final 5 round (including a pre-recorded Power of Veto competition and live eviction) then the final Head of Household competition is played in one part where the Final Head of Household wins the power to evict two HouseGuests in order to reduce the number of contestants inside the House down to two.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
After the first season of the British version of _Big Brother_ proved to be a success in the ratings for Channel 4, the network collaborated with the BBC for the first British season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ in aid of Comic Relief. The season ran for a condensed run of eight days and featured six British celebrities moving into the house used for the first British season.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-24) Due to the success of the first celebrity edition, a second season was ordered and shown exclusively on Channel 4 in November 2002. The celebrity version took a two-year break before returning for its third season in 2005 and became a regular staple alongside the regular British version. Starting with the third season, the show began to feature celebrities outside the United Kingdom alongside well-known British celebrities. Many notable American celebrities have since taken part in the British version of _Celebrity Big Brother_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-GlobalTV-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-AmericansInUKCBB-2-26) American actor Gary Busey took part in the fourteenth season in the summer of 2014 and became the first American celebrity to win _Celebrity Big Brother_ in the United Kingdom.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-Gary_Wins-27)
Julie Chen Moonves has hosted the series since its premiere.

### Differences from _Big Brother_
An American version of _Celebrity Big Brother_ has been speculated since 2002, along with a celebrity version of _Survivor._[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-2002-1-28) In an interview, Julie Chen and then CEO of CBS Corporation Leslie Moonves revealed talks of a celebrity edition of _Big Brother_ as far back as _Big Brother 2._[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-29) It was rumored that CBS was looking to air a celebrity edition in the fall after _Big Brother 3_ with radio personality Howard Stern speculated as a possible Houseguest.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-2002-2-30) Chen revealed that Paris Hilton had agreed to do it and Roseanne Barr initially agreed to take part, but then backed out.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-29) Barr would later take part in another celebrity spin-off of _Big Brother_ called _Big Brother: Celebrity Hijack_ in the United Kingdom in 2008, where she watched over a group of non-celebrity housemates for a day, set tasks and talked to them in the Diary Room.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Roseanne-BBCH-31) Julie Chen announced on September 7, 2017, during a live double eviction episode of _Big Brother 19_ that _Celebrity Big Brother_ would air sometime during the winter, before the twentieth season of _Big Brother_ in the summer of 2018.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-32)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
CBS confirmed that Chen would reprise her role as host for the celebrity edition with executive producers Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan returning. CBS also confirmed that the celebrity edition would be produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Press1-33) In an interview Chen revealed that her husband Les Moonves forced her to take a pay cut for _Celebrity Big Brother_ due to it being a condensed version.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-tvguide-34) Chen returned as the host for the second season now being credited as Julie Chen Moonves.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-JCReturn-35)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
Don Wollman and Clayton Halsey also reprises their roles as a co-executive producer and editor respectively.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ClosingCredits-36) Wollman also serves as the voice of Big Brother where he pre-records a series of statements that are played over the loud speakers inside the House. These range from asking HouseGuests to come to the Diary Room or reminding them they are not allowed to talk about production and their Diary Room sessions with other HouseGuests. Occasionally Wollman will make announcements to the HouseGuests that are not pre-recorded. Wollman's voice is primarily heard on the live Internet feeds while occasionally heard on the episodes.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-41) Halsey also serves as the narrator for the opening and closings of the broadcast episodes. In this role he recaps recent events that were aired in previous episodes during the opening while explaining what events will take place in future episodes during the closing.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Voices-38)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ClosingCredits2-37)

May 6, 2024 Updated May 7, 2024, 3:27 p.m. ET
"Big Brother" is around the corner.
The long-running CBS show is returning for a 26th season. But when does the summer staple premiere?
Here's everything we know so far.

## When is the 'Big Brother' 2024 premiere?
Fans finally have a premiere date for the 26th season. Parade Magazine's Sharon Tharp reported Tuesday that the two-night season premiere will air **July 17 and 18**.

## Will there be returning houseguests on 'Big Brother 26'?
No. CBS confirmed it will be new houseguests, per Tharp.

## What days will 'Big Brother' 2024 air?
The show will air Sundays, Wednesdays and Thursdays this year, all starting at 9 p.m. ET, per the popular "Big Brother" fan blog Hamster Watch.

## How many seasons of 'Big Brother' are there?
Technically, there are 25 seasons of "Big Brother." But there have been three seasons of "Celebrity Big Brother," which host Julie Chen Moonves recently told Us Weekly she expects to return during an upcoming winter. There was also one season of the spinoff series "Big Brother: Over the Top," and the "Big Brother Reindeer Games" holiday special aired for the first time last year.

May 6, 2024 Updated May 7, 2024, 3:27 p.m. ET
"Big Brother" is around the corner.
The long-running CBS show is returning for a 26th season. But when does the summer staple premiere?
Here's everything we know so far.
texts.1:
## When is the 'Big Brother' 2024 premiere?
Fans finally have a premiere date for the 26th season. Parade Magazine's Sharon Tharp reported Tuesday that the two-night season premiere will air **July 17 and 18**.
texts.2:
## Will there be returning houseguests on 'Big Brother 26'?
No. CBS confirmed it will be new houseguests, per Tharp.
texts.3:
## What days will 'Big Brother' 2024 air?
The show will air Sundays, Wednesdays and Thursdays this year, all starting at 9 p.m. ET, per the popular "Big Brother" fan blog Hamster Watch.
texts.4:
## How many seasons of 'Big Brother' are there?
Technically, there are 25 seasons of "Big Brother." But there have been three seasons of "Celebrity Big Brother," which host Julie Chen Moonves recently told Us Weekly she expects to return during an upcoming winter. There was also one season of the spinoff series "Big Brother: Over the Top," and the "Big Brother Reindeer Games" holiday special aired for the first time last year.

Fans finally have a premiere date for the 26th season. Parade Magazine's Sharon Tharp reported Tuesday that the two-night season premiere will air **July 17 and 18**.

No. CBS confirmed it will be new houseguests, per Tharp.

The show will air Sundays, Wednesdays and Thursdays this year, all starting at 9 p.m. ET, per the popular "Big Brother" fan blog Hamster Watch.

Technically, there are 25 seasons of "Big Brother." That is the official 14-person base. Yet the actual premiere may expand the board. CBS has teased surprise houseguests, and several outlets placed extra reality-TV names in the pre-premiere conversation before the first eviction cycle even began.

## Rick Devens, Angela Murray, and the Reality-TV Crossover Watch
The biggest pre-premiere twist is Rick Devens moving from _Survivor_ to _Big Brother_. The _Survivor: Edge of Extinction_ and _Survivor 50_ player will compete in Season 28. Devens is 42 and from Macon, Georgia.
Devens became a _Survivor_ name in 2019 after being voted out on day 11, winning his way back through the Edge of Extinction twist, finding idols, winning challenges, and losing fire-making to eventual winner Chris Underwood. On _Survivor 50_, he joined after the cast expanded to 24 people. His run included the MrBeast coin twist, immunity at two Tribal Councils, and a prize-money jump to $2 million, which Aubry Bracco eventually won. Devens finished seventh.
A second former _Survivor_ castaway is also expected in Season 28, though CBS and producers had not confirmed that identity before the premiere. Pre-premiere coverage also placed _Big Brother 26_ fan favorite Angela Murray, 52, from Long Beach, California, in the house. Rumors around _Survivor 46_ champion Dee Valladares, with Sharon Tharp tied to that reporting, also circulated before premiere night. Those names should be treated as reported, not fully CBS-confirmed, until they appear on air.
The franchise crossover history is already strange enough. Cirie Fields played _Big Brother_ Season 25 with her son, Jared Fields. Hayden Moss won _Big Brother 12_ before reaching sixth place on _Survivor: Blood vs. Water_. Caleb “Beast Mode Cowboy” Reynolds went from _Big Brother 16_ to _Survivor: Kaoh Rong_ and _Survivor: Game Changers_. Zach Wurtenberger watched his brother Cory Wurtenberger play _Big Brother 25_, while Russell Hantz’s brother Willie Hantz was expelled from _Big Brother 14_ after charging and pushing Joe Arvin.

## Prize Money, Host, and What Season 27 Leaves Behind
Julie Chen Moonves returns as host, a role she has held since _Big Brother_ began in 2000. The Season 28 grand prize remains $750,000.
Season 27 ended with Ashley Hollis, a 26-year-old attorney, winning that $750,000 prize. She defeated unemployed superfan Vince Panaro by a 6-1 jury vote. That result matters for Season 28 because the new cast includes several people who look socially polished enough to avoid early chaos, but competitive enough to keep the jury math unstable.
The early shape of Season 28 is therefore clear. CBS wants nostalgia, reality-TV crossover heat, a live-feed expansion, and a cast that can sell both competition and confessionals. For anyone tracking Big Brother 2026, the starting answer is July 9. The better question is how long the first-night cast remains the real cast.

That is the official 14-person base. Yet the actual premiere may expand the board. CBS has teased surprise houseguests, and several outlets placed extra reality-TV names in the pre-premiere conversation before the first eviction cycle even began.

## Rick Devens, Angela Murray, and the Reality-TV Crossover Watch
The biggest pre-premiere twist is Rick Devens moving from _Survivor_ to _Big Brother_. The _Survivor: Edge of Extinction_ and _Survivor 50_ player will compete in Season 28. Devens is 42 and from Macon, Georgia.
Devens became a _Survivor_ name in 2019 after being voted out on day 11, winning his way back through the Edge of Extinction twist, finding idols, winning challenges, and losing fire-making to eventual winner Chris Underwood. On _Survivor 50_, he joined after the cast expanded to 24 people. His run included the MrBeast coin twist, immunity at two Tribal Councils, and a prize-money jump to $2 million, which Aubry Bracco eventually won. Devens finished seventh.
A second former _Survivor_ castaway is also expected in Season 28, though CBS and producers had not confirmed that identity before the premiere. Pre-premiere coverage also placed _Big Brother 26_ fan favorite Angela Murray, 52, from Long Beach, California, in the house. Rumors around _Survivor 46_ champion Dee Valladares, with Sharon Tharp tied to that reporting, also circulated before premiere night. Those names should be treated as reported, not fully CBS-confirmed, until they appear on air.
The franchise crossover history is already strange enough. Cirie Fields played _Big Brother_ Season 25 with her son, Jared Fields. Hayden Moss won _Big Brother 12_ before reaching sixth place on _Survivor: Blood vs. Water_. Caleb “Beast Mode Cowboy” Reynolds went from _Big Brother 16_ to _Survivor: Kaoh Rong_ and _Survivor: Game Changers_. Zach Wurtenberger watched his brother Cory Wurtenberger play _Big Brother 25_, while Russell Hantz’s brother Willie Hantz was expelled from _Big Brother 14_ after charging and pushing Joe Arvin.

## Prize Money, Host, and What Season 27 Leaves Behind
Julie Chen Moonves returns as host, a role she has held since _Big Brother_ began in 2000. The Season 28 grand prize remains $750,000.
Season 27 ended with Ashley Hollis, a 26-year-old attorney, winning that $750,000 prize. She defeated unemployed superfan Vince Panaro by a 6-1 jury vote. That result matters for Season 28 because the new cast includes several people who look socially polished enough to avoid early chaos, but competitive enough to keep the jury math unstable.
The early shape of Season 28 is therefore clear. CBS wants nostalgia, reality-TV crossover heat, a live-feed expansion, and a cast that can sell both competition and confessionals. For anyone tracking Big Brother 2026, the starting answer is July 9. The better question is how long the first-night cast remains the real cast.

## Broadcast and coverage
The first season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was often reported on by various media outlets for the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her discussions about her time in the Trump administration.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-76) Reed Gaudens of _Fansided_ reviewed the series premiere positively noting the series "could either be so bad it’s good or just plain bad. Thankfully, it’s the former" while saying of the HouseGuests "weren’t exactly the famous faces we anticipated" for the season.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-77)Andy Dehnart of _Reality Blurred_ was more critical of the show noting that most of the season one Houseguests were previously on other reality shows like _Dancing with the Stars_ and _The Celebrity Apprentice_.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-78) In a post season review he noted the first season had been a "delight" when compared to a season of _Big Brother_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-79)

## Broadcast and coverage
_Celebrity Big Brother_ had a strong series premiere with the highest ratings since the premiere of _Big Brother 13_ on July 7, 2011. The series debuted to 7.27 million viewers with a 1.8/7 rating in the 18-49 demographic.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1E1_Rating-80) The remainder of the first season was scheduled as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The first season finale aired on February 25, 2018 with 5.2 million viewers with a 1.4/5 rating in the 18-49 demographic coming in second behind the closing ceremony for the Olympics.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-81) The first season averaged 5.04 million viewers per episode.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1AVG-82)
The second season premiere was down compared to the first season with 5.36 million viewers with a 1.4/6 in the 18-49 demographic.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E1_Rating-83) The eighth episode of the second season pulled in the lowest ratings of the season with 3.28 million viewers.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-84) The finale for the second season was watched by 3.87 million viewers which was below season average levels for the program.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E13_Rating-85) The second season averaged a total of 4.40 million viewers.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2AVG-86)

Title: ‘Celebrity Big Brother’ Premiere Can’t Push CBS Past NBC’s ‘Chicago’ Reruns in Total Viewers
Chunks: 0,1
“Celebrity Big Brother” was Wednesday’s highest-rated show among adults 18-49, but it didn’t draw enough eyeballs (of any age) to push CBS past NBC and its “One Chicago Reruns.” Don’t blame “Big Brother” or “The Amazing Race,” however, it was 10 o’clock’s “Good Sam” episode that dragged CBS’ primetime averages down. Still, with “Chicago Med,” “Fire” and “P.D.” in repeats, CBS was No. 1 in the key demo in terms of primetime ratings averages.
ABC and Fox bested the NBC encores in the key demo. The CW didn’t do any damage to the other nets last night, but it had a nice evening grading on a curve.
Both of The CW’s primetime hours (The CW and Fox do not nationally program the 10 p.m. hour; ABC, CBS and NBC do) last night rose double digits on a percentage basis to season-high viewership. “Legends of Tomorrow” drew its largest audience since June 2020 and “Batwoman” posted its best overall viewership since last April. All told, last night was The CW’s most-watched Wednesday since early August.
CBS was first in ratings with a 0.6 rating in the advertiser-coveted 18-49 demographic and second in total viewers with an average of 3.25 million, according to preliminary numbers.The “Big Brother – Celebrity Edition” premiere at 8 drew a 0.7 rating and 3.7 million total viewers. It was the night’s highest-rated individual program in the demo. At 9, “The Amazing Race” received a 0.6 rating and 3.6 million total viewers. “Good Sam” at 10 settled for a 0.3 rating and 2.5 million total viewers.
ABC and Fox tied for second in ratings, both with a 0.4. ABC was third in total viewers with 2.5 million, Fox was fourth with 2.2 million.

For ABC, “The Goldbergs” at 8 landed a 0.6 rating and 3.4 million total viewers. At 8:30, “The Wonder Years” posted a 0.5 rating and 2.3 million total viewers. “The Conners” at 9 earned a 0.5 rating and 3.2 million total viewers. At 9:30, “Home Economics” had a 0.4 rating and 2.1 million total viewers. “The Chase” at 10 got a 0.3 rating and 2.1 million total viewers.
For Fox, “I Can See Your Voice” at 8 had a 0.4 rating and 2.4 million total viewers. At 9, “Next Level Chef” got a 0.4 rating and 2 million total viewers.
NBC was fourth in ratings with a 0.3, but first in total viewers with 3.30 million, airing the trio of repeats.
The CW was fifth in ratings with a 0.1 and in total viewers with 608,000. “DC’s Legends of Tomorrow” at 8 had a 0.1 rating and 678,000 total viewers. At 9, “Batwoman” got a 0.1 and 538,000 total viewers.
We do not have early Nielsen numbers for Spanish-language broadcast networks Univision and Telemundo.

## Broadcast and coverage
The first season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was often reported on by various media outlets for the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her discussions about her time in the Trump administration.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-76) Reed Gaudens of _Fansided_ reviewed the series premiere positively noting the series "could either be so bad it’s good or just plain bad. Thankfully, it’s the former" while saying of the HouseGuests "weren’t exactly the famous faces we anticipated" for the season.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-77)Andy Dehnart of _Reality Blurred_ was more critical of the show noting that most of the season one Houseguests were previously on other reality shows like _Dancing with the Stars_ and _The Celebrity Apprentice_.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-78) In a post season review he noted the first season had been a "delight" when compared to a season of _Big Brother_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-79)
texts.23:
## Broadcast and coverage
_Celebrity Big Brother_ had a strong series premiere with the highest ratings since the premiere of _Big Brother 13_ on July 7, 2011. The series debuted to 7.27 million viewers with a 1.8/7 rating in the 18-49 demographic.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1E1_Rating-80) The remainder of the first season was scheduled as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The first season finale aired on February 25, 2018 with 5.2 million viewers with a 1.4/5 rating in the 18-49 demographic coming in second behind the closing ceremony for the Olympics.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-81) The first season averaged 5.04 million viewers per episode.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1AVG-82)
The second season premiere was down compared to the first season with 5.36 million viewers with a 1.4/6 in the 18-49 demographic.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E1_Rating-83) The eighth episode of the second season pulled in the lowest ratings of the season with 3.28 million viewers.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-84) The finale for the second season was watched by 3.87 million viewers which was below season average levels for the program.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E13_Rating-85) The second season averaged a total of 4.40 million viewers.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2AVG-86)

## Broadcast and coverage
The first season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was often reported on by various media outlets for the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her discussions about her time in the Trump administration.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-76) Reed Gaudens of _Fansided_ reviewed the series premiere positively noting the series "could either be so bad it’s good or just plain bad. Thankfully, it’s the former" while saying of the HouseGuests "weren’t exactly the famous faces we anticipated" for the season.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-77)Andy Dehnart of _Reality Blurred_ was more critical of the show noting that most of the season one Houseguests were previously on other reality shows like _Dancing with the Stars_ and _The Celebrity Apprentice_.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-78) In a post season review he noted the first season had been a "delight" when compared to a season of _Big Brother_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-79)

## Broadcast and coverage
_Celebrity Big Brother_ had a strong series premiere with the highest ratings since the premiere of _Big Brother 13_ on July 7, 2011. The series debuted to 7.27 million viewers with a 1.8/7 rating in the 18-49 demographic.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1E1_Rating-80) The remainder of the first season was scheduled as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The first season finale aired on February 25, 2018 with 5.2 million viewers with a 1.4/5 rating in the 18-49 demographic coming in second behind the closing ceremony for the Olympics.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-81) The first season averaged 5.04 million viewers per episode.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1AVG-82)
The second season premiere was down compared to the first season with 5.36 million viewers with a 1.4/6 in the 18-49 demographic.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E1_Rating-83) The eighth episode of the second season pulled in the lowest ratings of the season with 3.28 million viewers.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-84) The finale for the second season was watched by 3.87 million viewers which was below season average levels for the program.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E13_Rating-85) The second season averaged a total of 4.40 million viewers.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2AVG-86)

Title: ‘Celebrity Big Brother’ Premiere Can’t Push CBS Past NBC’s ‘Chicago’ Reruns in Total Viewers
Chunks: 0,1
“Celebrity Big Brother” was Wednesday’s highest-rated show among adults 18-49, but it didn’t draw enough eyeballs (of any age) to push CBS past NBC and its “One Chicago Reruns.” Don’t blame “Big Brother” or “The Amazing Race,” however, it was 10 o’clock’s “Good Sam” episode that dragged CBS’ primetime averages down. Still, with “Chicago Med,” “Fire” and “P.D.” in repeats, CBS was No. 1 in the key demo in terms of primetime ratings averages.
ABC and Fox bested the NBC encores in the key demo. The CW didn’t do any damage to the other nets last night, but it had a nice evening grading on a curve.
Both of The CW’s primetime hours (The CW and Fox do not nationally program the 10 p.m. hour; ABC, CBS and NBC do) last night rose double digits on a percentage basis to season-high viewership. “Legends of Tomorrow” drew its largest audience since June 2020 and “Batwoman” posted its best overall viewership since last April. All told, last night was The CW’s most-watched Wednesday since early August.
CBS was first in ratings with a 0.6 rating in the advertiser-coveted 18-49 demographic and second in total viewers with an average of 3.25 million, according to preliminary numbers.The “Big Brother – Celebrity Edition” premiere at 8 drew a 0.7 rating and 3.7 million total viewers. It was the night’s highest-rated individual program in the demo. At 9, “The Amazing Race” received a 0.6 rating and 3.6 million total viewers. “Good Sam” at 10 settled for a 0.3 rating and 2.5 million total viewers.
ABC and Fox tied for second in ratings, both with a 0.4. ABC was third in total viewers with 2.5 million, Fox was fourth with 2.2 million.

For ABC, “The Goldbergs” at 8 landed a 0.6 rating and 3.4 million total viewers. At 8:30, “The Wonder Years” posted a 0.5 rating and 2.3 million total viewers. “The Conners” at 9 earned a 0.5 rating and 3.2 million total viewers. At 9:30, “Home Economics” had a 0.4 rating and 2.1 million total viewers. “The Chase” at 10 got a 0.3 rating and 2.1 million total viewers.
For Fox, “I Can See Your Voice” at 8 had a 0.4 rating and 2.4 million total viewers. At 9, “Next Level Chef” got a 0.4 rating and 2 million total viewers.
NBC was fourth in ratings with a 0.3, but first in total viewers with 3.30 million, airing the trio of repeats.
The CW was fifth in ratings with a 0.1 and in total viewers with 608,000. “DC’s Legends of Tomorrow” at 8 had a 0.1 rating and 678,000 total viewers. At 9, “Batwoman” got a 0.1 and 538,000 total viewers.
We do not have early Nielsen numbers for Spanish-language broadcast networks Univision and Telemundo.

## Broadcast and coverage
The first season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was often reported on by various media outlets for the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her discussions about her time in the Trump administration.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-76) Reed Gaudens of _Fansided_ reviewed the series premiere positively noting the series "could either be so bad it’s good or just plain bad. Thankfully, it’s the former" while saying of the HouseGuests "weren’t exactly the famous faces we anticipated" for the season.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-77)Andy Dehnart of _Reality Blurred_ was more critical of the show noting that most of the season one Houseguests were previously on other reality shows like _Dancing with the Stars_ and _The Celebrity Apprentice_.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-78) In a post season review he noted the first season had been a "delight" when compared to a season of _Big Brother_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-79)

## Broadcast and coverage
_Celebrity Big Brother_ had a strong series premiere with the highest ratings since the premiere of _Big Brother 13_ on July 7, 2011. The series debuted to 7.27 million viewers with a 1.8/7 rating in the 18-49 demographic.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1E1_Rating-80) The remainder of the first season was scheduled as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The first season finale aired on February 25, 2018 with 5.2 million viewers with a 1.4/5 rating in the 18-49 demographic coming in second behind the closing ceremony for the Olympics.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-81) The first season averaged 5.04 million viewers per episode.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1AVG-82)
The second season premiere was down compared to the first season with 5.36 million viewers with a 1.4/6 in the 18-49 demographic.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E1_Rating-83) The eighth episode of the second season pulled in the lowest ratings of the season with 3.28 million viewers.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-84) The finale for the second season was watched by 3.87 million viewers which was below season average levels for the program.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E13_Rating-85) The second season averaged a total of 4.40 million viewers.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2AVG-86)

opened.information:
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)
Title: Celebrity Big Brother 1 (American season)
Chunks: 10,11,12,13,14
Julie Chen announced on September 7, 2017, during a live double eviction episode of _Big Brother 19_ that _Celebrity Big Brother_ would air sometime during the winter, before the twentieth season of _Big Brother_ in the summer of 2018. CBS later confirmed via a press release that Julie Chen would return to host the new season, and Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan will be executive producers. The season will be produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)
On September 13, 2017, it was revealed by Chen that her husband, CBS chief executive Leslie Moonves, forced her to take a pay cut for the celebrity edition to happen. Moonves stated, "You shouldn't be expected to be paid as if it's a full series. It's a condensed version."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvguide-50)
The format of the show remained similar to the American version of _Big Brother_. Competitions for Head of Household and Power of Veto had been confirmed to returned for this edition along with live evictions.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvline-2) On December 1, 2017, CBS revealed that the series would premiere on February 7, 2018, and wrap on February 25, 2018.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-51)

_Celebrity Big Brother_ was a condensed version of the game and would not last as long as a regular season of _Big Brother_, with episodes only shown over two weeks instead of three months.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvguide-50)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-52) Unlike the parent series Jury members were not sequestered separately and were allowed to return to the outside world as well as watch the show.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-53)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-54) Beginning with an incident that led to a lawsuit in _Big Brother 2_ when HouseGuest Justin Sebik got drunk and threatened fellow HouseGuest Krista Stegall by holding a knife to her throat, there has been an alcohol restriction in the house.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-55)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-56) The alcohol restriction was lifted for the Celebrity HouseGuests.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-57)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-58) The space in the backyard was reduced to allow production to constantly perform construction for competitions but still allow 24/7 access for the HouseGuests.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-59) For the celebrity version of America's Favorite HouseGuest,

the term Favorite Celebrity HouseGuest was also being used interchangeably.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-60)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-61) For the first time since the beginning of the American series, five players were featured in the season's finale night versus the usual three.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-62)

The main television coverage of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was screened on CBS during the winter of the 2017–18 network television season. CBS decided to schedule the spin-off during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49) Episodes aired on Sundays, Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays with two special episodes on Thursday, February 8 and Saturday, February 24. Most episodes aired for one hour and aired from 8:00–9:00 p.m. EST; the Friday episodes and the season finale, however, ran for two hours each (from 8:00–10:00 p.m. EST).[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Air_dates-63) The live Internet feeds returned for the American version of _Celebrity Big Brother_ as part of CBS All Access.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-46) Alongside the weekly shows on CBS, the companion series _Big Brother: After Dark_ returned on Pop under the title _Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark_. The show provided live coverage nightly from inside the House.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-64)

#### International broadcasts
[edit]
Promotional logo created for use in Australia that resembles the logo of Australian adaptation of _Big Brother_ from 2012 to 2014.
Global announced on December 20, 2017, that the broadcaster had acquired the rights to air _Celebrity Big Brother_ in Canada.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Broadcast-GlobalCAN-65) Global has broadcast the American version of _Big Brother_ since its launch in 2000.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-BBCPR-66)Nine Network confirmed they would air the season in Australia under the name _Celebrity Big Brother U.S._.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Australia-1-67) Nine created a special logo for the show resembling the eye logo of the ninth through eleventh seasons of Australian adaptation that previously aired on the network.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-68) Episodes were "fast-tracked" and available on their streaming service 9Now shortly after their American airing with televised broadcast on 9Go! starting February 11, 2018.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Australia-1-67) Due to low ratings episodes were moved from the 9:30pm timeslot to 11:30pm effective February 14, 2018.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-69)

texts.10:
Julie Chen announced on September 7, 2017, during a live double eviction episode of _Big Brother 19_ that _Celebrity Big Brother_ would air sometime during the winter, before the twentieth season of _Big Brother_ in the summer of 2018. CBS later confirmed via a press release that Julie Chen would return to host the new season, and Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan will be executive producers. The season will be produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)
On September 13, 2017, it was revealed by Chen that her husband, CBS chief executive Leslie Moonves, forced her to take a pay cut for the celebrity edition to happen. Moonves stated, "You shouldn't be expected to be paid as if it's a full series. It's a condensed version."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvguide-50)
The format of the show remained similar to the American version of _Big Brother_. Competitions for Head of Household and Power of Veto had been confirmed to returned for this edition along with live evictions.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvline-2) On December 1, 2017, CBS revealed that the series would premiere on February 7, 2018, and wrap on February 25, 2018.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-51)
texts.11: _Celebrity Big Brother_ was a condensed version of the game and would not last as long as a regular season of _Big Brother_, with episodes only shown over two weeks instead of three months.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvguide-50)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-52) Unlike the parent series Jury members were not sequestered separately and were allowed to return to the outside world as well as watch the show.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-53)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-54) Beginning with an incident that led to a lawsuit in _Big Brother 2_ when HouseGuest Justin Sebik got drunk and threatened fellow HouseGuest Krista Stegall by holding a knife to her throat, there has been an alcohol restriction in the house.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-55)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-56) The alcohol restriction was lifted for the Celebrity HouseGuests.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-57)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-58) The space in the backyard was reduced to allow production to constantly perform construction for competitions but still allow 24/7 access for the HouseGuests.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-59) For the celebrity version of America's Favorite HouseGuest,
texts.12: the term Favorite Celebrity HouseGuest was also being used interchangeably.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-60)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-61) For the first time since the beginning of the American series, five players were featured in the season's finale night versus the usual three.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-62)
texts.13: The main television coverage of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was screened on CBS during the winter of the 2017–18 network television season. CBS decided to schedule the spin-off during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49) Episodes aired on Sundays, Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays with two special episodes on Thursday, February 8 and Saturday, February 24. Most episodes aired for one hour and aired from 8:00–9:00 p.m. EST; the Friday episodes and the season finale, however, ran for two hours each (from 8:00–10:00 p.m. EST).[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Air_dates-63) The live Internet feeds returned for the American version of _Celebrity Big Brother_ as part of CBS All Access.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-46) Alongside the weekly shows on CBS, the companion series _Big Brother: After Dark_ returned on Pop under the title _Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark_. The show provided live coverage nightly from inside the House.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-64)
texts.14:
#### International broadcasts
[edit]
Promotional logo created for use in Australia that resembles the logo of Australian adaptation of _Big Brother_ from 2012 to 2014.
Global announced on December 20, 2017, that the broadcaster had acquired the rights to air _Celebrity Big Brother_ in Canada.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Broadcast-GlobalCAN-65) Global has broadcast the American version of _Big Brother_ since its launch in 2000.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-BBCPR-66)Nine Network confirmed they would air the season in Australia under the name _Celebrity Big Brother U.S._.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Australia-1-67) Nine created a special logo for the show resembling the eye logo of the ninth through eleventh seasons of Australian adaptation that previously aired on the network.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-68) Episodes were "fast-tracked" and available on their streaming service 9Now shortly after their American airing with televised broadcast on 9Go! starting February 11, 2018.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Australia-1-67) Due to low ratings episodes were moved from the 9:30pm timeslot to 11:30pm effective February 14, 2018.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-69)

## Broadcast and coverage
The first season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was often reported on by various media outlets for the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her discussions about her time in the Trump administration.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-76) Reed Gaudens of _Fansided_ reviewed the series premiere positively noting the series "could either be so bad it’s good or just plain bad. Thankfully, it’s the former" while saying of the HouseGuests "weren’t exactly the famous faces we anticipated" for the season.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-77)Andy Dehnart of _Reality Blurred_ was more critical of the show noting that most of the season one Houseguests were previously on other reality shows like _Dancing with the Stars_ and _The Celebrity Apprentice_.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-78) In a post season review he noted the first season had been a "delight" when compared to a season of _Big Brother_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-79)
texts.23:
## Broadcast and coverage
_Celebrity Big Brother_ had a strong series premiere with the highest ratings since the premiere of _Big Brother 13_ on July 7, 2011. The series debuted to 7.27 million viewers with a 1.8/7 rating in the 18-49 demographic.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1E1_Rating-80) The remainder of the first season was scheduled as counterprogramming to NBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The first season finale aired on February 25, 2018 with 5.2 million viewers with a 1.4/5 rating in the 18-49 demographic coming in second behind the closing ceremony for the Olympics.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-81) The first season averaged 5.04 million viewers per episode.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S1AVG-82)
The second season premiere was down compared to the first season with 5.36 million viewers with a 1.4/6 in the 18-49 demographic.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E1_Rating-83) The eighth episode of the second season pulled in the lowest ratings of the season with 3.28 million viewers.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-84) The finale for the second season was watched by 3.87 million viewers which was below season average levels for the program.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2E13_Rating-85) The second season averaged a total of 4.40 million viewers.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-S2AVG-86)

Julie Chen announced on September 7, 2017, during a live double eviction episode of _Big Brother 19_ that _Celebrity Big Brother_ would air sometime during the winter, before the twentieth season of _Big Brother_ in the summer of 2018. CBS later confirmed via a press release that Julie Chen would return to host the new season, and Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan will be executive producers. The season will be produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)
On September 13, 2017, it was revealed by Chen that her husband, CBS chief executive Leslie Moonves, forced her to take a pay cut for the celebrity edition to happen. Moonves stated, "You shouldn't be expected to be paid as if it's a full series. It's a condensed version."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvguide-50)
The format of the show remained similar to the American version of _Big Brother_. Competitions for Head of Household and Power of Veto had been confirmed to returned for this edition along with live evictions.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvline-2) On December 1, 2017, CBS revealed that the series would premiere on February 7, 2018, and wrap on February 25, 2018.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-51)

_Celebrity Big Brother_ was a condensed version of the game and would not last as long as a regular season of _Big Brother_, with episodes only shown over two weeks instead of three months.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvguide-50)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-52) Unlike the parent series Jury members were not sequestered separately and were allowed to return to the outside world as well as watch the show.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-53)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-54) Beginning with an incident that led to a lawsuit in _Big Brother 2_ when HouseGuest Justin Sebik got drunk and threatened fellow HouseGuest Krista Stegall by holding a knife to her throat, there has been an alcohol restriction in the house.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-55)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-56) The alcohol restriction was lifted for the Celebrity HouseGuests.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-57)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-58) The space in the backyard was reduced to allow production to constantly perform construction for competitions but still allow 24/7 access for the HouseGuests.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-59) For the celebrity version of America's Favorite HouseGuest,

the term Favorite Celebrity HouseGuest was also being used interchangeably.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-60)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-61) For the first time since the beginning of the American series, five players were featured in the season's finale night versus the usual three.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-62)

The main television coverage of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was screened on CBS during the winter of the 2017–18 network television season. CBS decided to schedule the spin-off during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49) Episodes aired on Sundays, Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays with two special episodes on Thursday, February 8 and Saturday, February 24. Most episodes aired for one hour and aired from 8:00–9:00 p.m. EST; the Friday episodes and the season finale, however, ran for two hours each (from 8:00–10:00 p.m. EST).[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Air_dates-63) The live Internet feeds returned for the American version of _Celebrity Big Brother_ as part of CBS All Access.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-46) Alongside the weekly shows on CBS, the companion series _Big Brother: After Dark_ returned on Pop under the title _Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark_. The show provided live coverage nightly from inside the House.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-64)
